title: Olympic Swimmer vs. Giant Fish: Who's Stronger?
summary:
Imagine swimming against a fish so strong it can pull a boat. That's what Olympic swimmer Caeleb Dressel did! He's won 9 gold medals, but could he beat some of the ocean's toughest fish in a tug-of-war?

In a YouTube video from BlacktipH, Dressel wore a harness attached to fishing lines. Each line had a different amount of drag—that's the force you need to pull against. He started with 8.5 pounds of drag and swam 50 yards. It felt like a 6 out of 10, he said.

Next, he tried 20 pounds of drag, like pulling a tuna. He did it, but it was harder—about 8.2 out of 10. Then came the big test: 50 pounds of drag, like a marlin. He swam butterfly, but only pulled six inches in 15 seconds! A real marlin can fight for an hour. With fins and paddles, he did better, pulling 10 yards.

His last challenge was 120 pounds of drag, like a Goliath grouper. That's super heavy! He tried swimming straight down, but only moved a few inches. Even the strongest swimmer can't beat these fish!

Dressel also caught a 7.5-pound Bonita fish before the tests. He had a fun side challenge: for each level he completed, he earned back his Olympic medals. His son watched him take on the marlin-level test, which made him want to win.

So, are fish stronger than Olympic swimmers? For now, yes! But Dressel showed he's super powerful in the water. Would you try this challenge?
why_it_matters: Next time you go swimming, you can appreciate how hard a swimmer's muscles have to work—and remember that ocean animals are some of the strongest athletes in nature.

background_read: Caeleb Dressel is an American Olympic swimmer who has won nine gold medals.
BlacktipH is a YouTube channel that makes fishing videos.
In this challenge, Dressel did not swim against a real fish; instead, the fishing line was set to different amounts of drag, or pull, to feel like fighting fish such as tuna, marlin, and grouper.
Article_Structure: WHO: Caeleb Dressel, a top Olympic swimmer, tried the challenge.
WHAT: He swam against heavier and heavier drag, from 8.5 pounds up to 120 pounds, to test his strength against ocean fish.
WHERE: In the water, in a YouTube video made by BlacktipH.
WHY: To see whether even an Olympic swimmer can pull as hard as powerful fish like marlin and Goliath grouper.

perspectives.description: Dressel makes the challenge fun and shows that trying again and pushing through hard pulls can help you keep going.
The test shows how incredibly strong ocean fish are: a fish like a marlin can keep fighting much longer than even an Olympic swimmer can.
Some people might say pulling against a fishing line is not the same as fighting a real fish, so the test only gives a rough idea of who is stronger.
